p:cNvPr.descr: The five stages of protein synthesis. This image is mainly a circle made up of arrows pointing to small and large subunits. The small subunits are orange and are mostly square but extend out at the top. The larger subunits are yellow and circular with a mostly flat bottom that dips down on the left side. Stage 1 is the activation of amino acids, where the tRNA is aminoacylated. The image begins with a green line intertwined on a square yellow base with an arrow on the right. This arrow has a blue sphere joining it and points to the same image with the sphere on top and to the right. To the right of this is a small subunit which joins an arrow pointing to the green image with the sphere on top, which is labeled as aminoacyl-tRNA. Flowing through the small subunit is a green line that originates with 5 (prime) and is light green. It turns right at the base of the aminacyl-tRNA and becomes dark green, then turns light green just after the base, and flows down and right, then horizontal once it is out of the subunit. Towards the right end it is red, then turns light green again. To the right of this is 3 (prime). This is stage 2: Initiation: the mRNA and the aminoacylated tRNA bind to the small ribosomal subunit. The large subunit then binds. This has a curved arrow pointing up and right with a large subunit joining it. The arrow points to the same image just described, but has a large subunit bonded on top. Below this is a curved arrow with the aminoacyl-tRNA joining it, which points to the same image as above, but now has two aminoacyl-tRNA images. An arrow on the left of this points left to the two sub units with only one aminoacyl-tRNA in the middle and a line of small blue spheres going up, then turning left, up, then right. The green line now attaches to the base of the aminacyl-tRNA just to the left of the red section, then flows down and left to horizontal. The dark green portion is now just right of the left end. This is stage 3: Elongation: successive cycles of aminoacyl-tRNA binding and peptide bond formation occur until the ribosome reaches a stop codon. To the left of the image is an arrow pointing up to the green mRNA line with the dark green section on the left signifying the start and the red section on the right, signifying stop. This is stage 4: Termination: Translation stops when a stop codon is encountered. The mRNA and protein dissociate, and the ribosomal subunits are recycled. This arrow has another arrow jut left to the large sub unit, the small subunit, and the blue spheres. Below the blue spheres is a down arrow to those spheres clustered in a circle. Below this is a down arrow with two hollow red circles joining it. This points to the cluster of blue spheres, with a hollow red circle at the top right and one at the bottom left. This is stage 5: Protein folding and posttranslational processing. From the mRNA line, the arrow points up to stage 1 again.
